public_rationale: For July–September 2026, Meta reported higher depreciation and amortization, higher net income and a separate $9.89 billion litigation charge [e1]. Alphabet reported higher depreciation and lower net income for the same quarter, with equity losses reducing current-quarter net income by $6.7 billion [e2]. These results cover a quarter that mostly precedes the September 22 forecast [e1, e2]. They do not isolate substantial depreciation-driven net-profit erosion across Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta, so they do not meet the early-resolution rule [e1, e2].
limitations: The evidence covers two of the four named companies and does not establish the required group-wide effect.
Meta's combined depreciation and amortization figure does not isolate depreciation.
Other material drivers of net income require reconciliation.
The forecast has no deadline or numerical threshold. A finite period without the predicted outcome cannot disprove it.

statement.excerpt: Hyperscalers have massive depreciation charges to look forward to that will eat their profits alive.

our_interpretation: Use Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon and Meta from the surrounding discussion.
The plain reading is that sharply higher depreciation will substantially erode net profits across the group, rather than merely appearing as an expense.
Net profits follows the surrounding reference to net income.
No numerical magnitude, deadline or accounting standard is expressly stated; company-reported financial results are implied.
The surrounding possibility of writing off GPUs is an alternative accounting outcome, not an antecedent that must occur.
criteria.support_condition: Realized post-publication results show large depreciation increases substantially eroding net profits across the named group, with the effect distinguished from other costs, taxes and investment gains or losses.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A finite period of strong profits does not disprove this undated forecast. Contradiction would require a decisive event eliminating the asserted future depreciation-and-profit outcome within the relevant investment cycle.
